---
title: "Scrape: malls"
engine: knitr
---

A Wikipedia category has no table (it's just a list of page links), so `rvest::html_table()` and `pandas.read_html()` have nothing to parse. The MediaWiki API's `categorymembers` endpoint returns the same list as structured JSON instead, and handles pagination with a `cmcontinue` token for categories over 500 members.

The code below fetches the defunct malls category and its two subcategories, then labels each page with the category it came from.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: scrape-malls-r
#| eval: false
library(httr2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

fetch_category_members <- function(category) {
  resps <- request("https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php") |>
    req_user_agent("wikimill-project/0.1") |>
    req_url_query(
      action = "query", list = "categorymembers",
      cmtitle = paste0("Category:", category), cmlimit = 500,
      format = "json"
    ) |>
    req_perform_iterative(
      next_req = iterate_with_cursor(
        "cmcontinue",
        resp_param_value = \(resp) resp_body_json(resp)$continue$cmcontinue
      ),
      max_reqs = Inf
    )
  titles <- resps_data(resps, \(resp) {
    vapply(resp_body_json(resp)$query$categorymembers, \(m) m$title, character(1))
  })
  tibble(title = titles)
}

categories <- c(
  "Defunct_shopping_malls_in_the_United_States" = "Defunct",
  "Demolished_shopping_malls_in_the_United_States" = "Demolished",
  "Abandoned_shopping_malls_in_the_United_States" = "Abandoned"
)
malls <- bind_rows(lapply(names(categories), \(cat) {
  fetch_category_members(cat) |> mutate(status = categories[[cat]])
}))
write_csv(malls, "data/defunct_malls.csv")
head(malls)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: scrape-malls-py
#| eval: false
import pandas as pd
import requests

API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"

def fetch_category_members(category):
    params = {
        "action": "query", "list": "categorymembers",
        "cmtitle": f"Category:{category}", "cmlimit": 500,
        "format": "json"
    }
    members = []
    while True:
        resp = requests.get(API, params=params, headers={"User-Agent": "wikimill-project/0.1"}).json()
        members.extend(resp["query"]["categorymembers"])
        if "continue" not in resp:
            break
        params["cmcontinue"] = resp["continue"]["cmcontinue"]
    return pd.DataFrame(members)[["title"]]

categories = {
    "Defunct_shopping_malls_in_the_United_States": "Defunct",
    "Demolished_shopping_malls_in_the_United_States": "Demolished",
    "Abandoned_shopping_malls_in_the_United_States": "Abandoned",
}
malls = pd.concat(
    [fetch_category_members(cat).assign(status=label) for cat, label in categories.items()],
    ignore_index=True
)
malls.to_csv("data/defunct_malls.csv", index=False)
malls.head()
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## httr2 has the edge

`req_perform_iterative()` with `iterate_with_cursor()` handles the `cmcontinue` loop for us, and `httr2` also ships `req_throttle()` and `req_retry()` for polite, rate-limited requests. With `requests`, the pagination loop, throttling, and retries are all code we write ourselves.
:::

These chunks are shown for reference only (`eval: false`), so rendering the site doesn't hit Wikipedia. Run `Rscript src/scrape_malls.R` or `python src/scrape_malls.py` from the project root to refresh `data/defunct_malls.csv`. See [clean_malls.qmd](clean_malls.qmd) for the next step.
